samf-senior-2017-r2-01.title: Fraction of an hour
samf-senior-2017-r2-01.body:
$12$ minutes is $\frac{12}{60}=\frac15$ of an hour, so the train travels $\frac15\times100=20$ km.

**Answer: 20**

samf-senior-2017-r2-02.title: Pigeonhole
samf-senior-2017-r2-02.body:
With two socks you could get one of each colour. With three socks, since there are only two colours, two must have the same colour. So $3$ socks are needed.

**Answer: 3**

samf-senior-2017-r2-03.title: Scale factor squared
samf-senior-2017-r2-03.body:
The enlarged quadrilateral is similar to the original with ratio $3$, so its area is $3^2\times16=144$.

**Answer: 144**

samf-senior-2017-r2-04.title: Average of first and last
samf-senior-2017-r2-04.body:
The numbers $2,4,\dots,200$ form an arithmetic sequence, so the average is $\frac{2+200}{2}=101$.

**Answer: 101**

samf-senior-2017-r2-06.title: Make powers of 10
samf-senior-2017-r2-06.body:
$2^{12}5^8=2^4\cdot(2\cdot5)^8=16\times10^8$, which is $16$ followed by eight zeros: $10$ digits.

**Answer: 10**

samf-senior-2017-r2-07.title: Quadrilateral APCQ
samf-senior-2017-r2-07.body:
The interior angles of quadrilateral $APCQ$ at $A$ and $C$ are $180^\circ-42^\circ=138^\circ$ and $180^\circ-38^\circ=142^\circ$ ($P,A,B$ and $P,C,D$ are straight). The angles at $P$ and $Q$ sum to $360^\circ-138^\circ-142^\circ=80^\circ$.

**Answer: 80**

samf-senior-2017-r2-07.title: Join PQ
samf-senior-2017-r2-07.body:
By the exterior angle theorem, $\angle BAQ=\angle APQ+\angle AQP$ and $\angle DCQ=\angle CPQ+\angle CQP$. Adding: $\angle BPD+\angle AQC=(\angle APQ+\angle CPQ)+(\angle AQP+\angle CQP)=42^\circ+38^\circ=80^\circ$.

**Answer: 80**

samf-senior-2017-r2-08.title: Difference of two triangles
samf-senior-2017-r2-08.body:
The arrowhead is a large triangle (apex $A$, base the bottom side of the square, area $\frac12\cdot4\cdot4=8$) minus the triangle with apex $B$ on the same base (height $2$, area $\frac12\cdot4\cdot2=4$). So the area is $8-4=4$.

**Answer: 4**

samf-senior-2017-r2-11.title: Product of the face areas
samf-senior-2017-r2-11.body:
If the edges are $x,y,z$ then the face areas are $xy,yz,zx$ and $(xyz)^2=84\cdot70\cdot30=176400=420^2$. So the volume is $xyz=420$.

**Answer: 420**

samf-senior-2017-r2-12.title: Use symmetry
samf-senior-2017-r2-12.body:
The figure has $180^\circ$ rotational symmetry about the centre, so the shaded region is half of what is left when the two circles are removed from the rectangle. If the shorter side is $x$ (the circle diameter), the rectangle is $2x\times x$ and the shaded area is $\frac12\left(2x^2-2\pi\frac{x^2}4\right)=x^2-\frac\pi4x^2$. Setting this equal to $100-25\pi$ gives $x^2=100$, $x=10$ and $AB=2x=20$.

**Answer: 20**

samf-senior-2017-r2-13.title: Exponent rules
samf-senior-2017-r2-13.body:
$r=(2\cdot3)^{2b}=36^b$. Also $r=3^bx^b=(3x)^b$. So $3x=36$ (for $b\neq0$ and positive bases) and $x=12$.

**Answer: 12**

samf-senior-2017-r2-14.title: Fractions of the total
samf-senior-2017-r2-14.body:
Let $n$ be the number of children. Red and green drinkers are $\frac12n+\frac13n=\frac56n$, so the remaining $\frac16n=15$ and $n=90$.

**Answer: 90**

samf-senior-2017-r2-15.title: Factor-count formula
samf-senior-2017-r2-15.body:
If $n=p_1^{e_1}p_2^{e_2}\cdots$ then $n$ has $(e_1+1)(e_2+1)\cdots$ factors. Since $5$ is prime, $n=p^4$. In $1$ to $100$: $2^4=16$ and $3^4=81$ ($5^4=625$ is too big). So $2$ numbers.

**Answer: 2**

samf-senior-2017-r2-15.title: Factors come in pairs
samf-senior-2017-r2-15.body:
Factors pair up as $d$ and $n/d$, so an odd number of factors forces $n$ to be a perfect square. Checking $1,4,9,\dots,100$: $16$ has factors $1,2,4,8,16$ and $81$ has $1,3,9,27,81$; the other squares have $1,3,7$ or $9$ factors. So $2$.

**Answer: 2**

samf-senior-2017-r2-16.title: Equation of the parabola
samf-senior-2017-r2-16.body:
Put the origin at $M$: the parabola has zeros at $x=\pm20$ and passes through $(0;16)$, so $y=a(x^2-400)$ with $-400a=16$, $a=-\frac1{25}$. At $x=5$: $y=16-\frac{25}{25}=15$.

**Answer: 15**

samf-senior-2017-r2-17.title: Probability times 60
samf-senior-2017-r2-17.body:
For a string of length $1$ cut at $x$, the longer piece is at least twice the shorter if $x\le\frac13$ or $x\ge\frac23$, which has probability $\frac23$. The expected number is $\frac23\times60=40$.

**Answer: 40**

samf-senior-2017-r2-18.title: Conditional probability
samf-senior-2017-r2-18.body:
There are $8$ equally likely boy/girl sequences; excluding BBB leaves $7$. Those with at least two girls: GGG, GGB, GBG, BGG: $4$. So the probability is $\frac47=\frac{32}{56}$ and $x=32$.

**Answer: 32**

samf-senior-2017-r2-20.title: Similar triangles
samf-senior-2017-r2-20.body:
Triangle $ADE$ is similar to $ABC$ and has area $1-\frac13=\frac23$ of it, so the ratio of corresponding sides is $\sqrt{\frac23}$. Then $DE=\sqrt{\tfrac23}\cdot192\sqrt6=192\sqrt4=384$.

**Answer: 384**

samf-senior-2017-r2-21.title: Count per vertex
samf-senior-2017-r2-21.body:
Each vertex lies on $3$ faces: two octagons and one triangle. Segments to the other vertices of these faces lie on the surface: $7+7+2=16$ vertices counted, minus $3$ counted twice (the neighbours along the shared edges) gives $13$. The remaining $23-13=10$ vertices give interior segments. Each segment is counted from both ends, so the number is $\frac{24\times10}2=120$.

**Answer: 120**

samf-senior-2017-r2-22.title: Difference of squares
samf-senior-2017-r2-22.body:
Let the populations be $x^2$, $x^2+100=y^2+1$ and $y^2+101=z^2$. Then $z^2-y^2=101$, a prime, so $(z-y)(z+y)=1\cdot101$, giving $z=51$, $y=50$. The 2015 population is $x^2=y^2+1-100=2500-99=2401$, with digit sum $2+4+0+1=7$.

**Answer: 7**

samf-senior-2017-r2-24.title: Cycle decomposition
samf-senior-2017-r2-24.body:
In one pass the card in position $1$ (the Ace) moves to position $2$ (the output is $6,A,7,\dots$), position $2$ goes to $5$, $5$ to $12$, $12$ to $10$, $10$ to $9$, $9$ to $6$ and $6$ back to position $1$: a cycle of length $7$ (A, 2, 5, Q, 10, 9, 6). Similarly $3\to13\to7\to3$ is a cycle of length $3$, position $4$ is fixed, and $8\to11\to8$ is a cycle of length $2$. The order returns after $\operatorname{lcm}(7,3,1,2)=42$ passes.

**Answer: 42**

samf-senior-2017-r2-25.title: Auxiliary point X
samf-senior-2017-r2-25.body:
By the exterior angle theorem in $\triangle AMC$, $\angle MAC=45^\circ-30^\circ=15^\circ$. Choose $X$ on $AC$ with $\angle MXC=30^\circ$. Then $\triangle MXC$ is isosceles with $MX=MC=MB$, so $X$ lies on the circle with diameter $BC$ (centre $M$) and $\angle BXC=90^\circ$. In $\triangle AMX$ the exterior angle at $X$ is $30^\circ=\angle MAX+\angle AMX$, so $\angle AMX=15^\circ=\angle MAX$ and $XA=XM$. Next $\angle BMX=45^\circ+15^\circ=60^\circ$ and $MB=MX$, so $\triangle BMX$ is equilateral and $XB=XM=XA$. Finally $\angle AXB=90^\circ$ (as $\angle BXC=90^\circ$), so $\triangle AXB$ is an isosceles right triangle and $\angle BAC=\angle BAX=45^\circ$.

**Answer: 45**

samf-senior-2017-r2-25.title: Coordinates
samf-senior-2017-r2-25.body:
Put $M=(0,0)$, $B=(-1,0)$, $C=(1,0)$. Since $\angle BMA=45^\circ$, $A=(-u,u)$ for some $u>0$. The condition $\angle ACB=30^\circ$ gives $\frac u{1+u}=\tan30^\circ=\frac1{\sqrt3}$, so $u=\frac{\sqrt3+1}2$. The vector $\overrightarrow{BA}=(1-u,\,u)$ has negative first coordinate (as $u>1$) and $\frac{u}{u-1}=\frac{\sqrt3+1}{\sqrt3-1}=2+\sqrt3=\tan75^\circ$, so $BA$ makes an angle of $75^\circ$ with the negative $x$-axis, i.e. $\angle ABC=180^\circ-75^\circ=105^\circ$. Therefore $\angle BAC=180^\circ-105^\circ-30^\circ=45^\circ$.

**Answer: 45**
